text: Jesus was born in Bethlehem during the reign of Herod the Great. The Gospel of Luke describes the journey from Nazareth to Bethlehem as necessitated by a census ordered by Caesar Augustus.

Archaeological excavations at Capernaum have uncovered the remains of a first-century house that was later enclosed within a fourth-century octagonal church structure. The site is traditionally identified as Peter's house.

The doctrine of the Trinity holds that God exists as three persons — Father, Son, and Holy Spirit — in one divine essence. This formulation was developed through the ecumenical councils of the fourth century.
The Synoptic Gospels are Matthew, Mark, and Luke. They are called synoptic because they can be viewed together in parallel columns, and they share substantial material in common.

The city of Jerusalem sits at an elevation of approximately 754 metres above sea level in the Judaean mountains. The city was the political and religious centre of Jewish life during the Second Temple period.
The apostle Peter, originally named Simon, was a fisherman from Bethsaida before becoming a disciple of Jesus. According to church tradition, he was martyred in Rome under Emperor Nero.
The Greek word logos appears in the prologue of John's Gospel and is typically translated as Word. The term carried rich connotations in both Jewish wisdom literature and Greek philosophy.
The Second Temple was extensively renovated and expanded by Herod the Great beginning around 20 BCE. The project employed thousands of labourers and took decades to complete.

The four canonical Gospels were accepted as authoritative by the early church by the end of the second century. Irenaeus of Lyons argued that there must be exactly four Gospels, corresponding to the four winds and the four living creatures of Revelation.
Jesus was crucified under Pontius Pilate, the Roman prefect of Judea. Crucifixion was a common form of capital punishment in the Roman Empire, reserved primarily for slaves and insurrectionists.

The resurrection of Jesus is the central claim of Christian faith. According to the New Testament, he appeared to his disciples on multiple occasions over a period of forty days before ascending to heaven.

The Gospel of Mark records that Jesus taught in parables, and when he was alone with his disciples he explained everything to them privately. Many of these parables use agricultural imagery drawn from everyday life in Galilee.
